next_steps: Measure a rule with and without it on the same inputs; a single count says nothing. And check what the consumer actually reads: the search ignores step rewards, so a reward test proves nothing about the search

A default in a classifier is a claim: 'minor' and 'at peace' were what the code said when it knew nothing. Read the owner's own UI code for every call before planning; two names the plan relied on did not exist there
Check what the producer actually sends before trusting a fixture: the search tests seeded enemy units the real exporter never exports by default (GM-B8)

A fallback that picks 'the first one' depends on an order nobody chose: name the order and test with more than one candidate. A mock has every attribute: detect a protocol on the class, not with hasattr

An event that is cleared before it is waited on loses whatever set it first: hand out by sequence number. And a fallback that makes an old value look current needs a check that the old value is still in force, not only that something is alive
Run the real loop against the real mod code before reviewing it: the stand-in as a GameBridge (tests/fixtures/lua_bridge.py) found a spin no reading had (research re-chosen after every choice)
A veto applied after the policy's choice costs a choice: filter the offers before asking
When a check becomes a gate (the executor's check now decides what is offered), re-read what it does when it cannot ask: fail-open that was tolerable on execution listed everything as an offer
A guard added to stop a loop can be the loop: test a cap together with the state it guards against (the per-turn cap trapped a blocked turn)
A stand-in written from the same reading as the code under test cannot catch a wrong reading: list those assumptions for the live check instead of calling them tested
Tests of a command assert on the game state after the next frame, never on a recorded call or the command's own answer
For a game API, read the game's own UI Lua first; a strict check the UI never asks is unverified even when the stand-in models it
Lua's %c asks the C library and differs on Windows: write byte ranges out
Base every follow-up PR on the default branch; when a PR merges, merge the default branch into the open ones and resolve doc conflicts there
